original_query: select s_name, count(*) as numwait from supplier, lineitem l1, orders, nation where s_suppkey = l1.l_suppkey and o_orderkey = l1.l_orderkey and o_orderstatus = 'F' and l1.l_receiptdate > l1.l_commitdate and exists ( select * from lineitem l2 where l2.l_orderkey = l1.l_orderkey and l2.l_suppkey <> l1.l_suppkey ) and not exists ( select * from lineitem l3 where l3.l_orderkey = l1.l_orderkey and l3.l_suppkey <> l1.l_suppkey and l3.l_receiptdate > l3.l_commitdate ) and s_nationkey = n_nationkey and n_name = 'MOZAMBIQUE' group by s_name order by numwait desc, s_name limit 100;
rewritten_query:
WITH candidate_orders AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT l1.l_orderkey
    FROM nation n
    JOIN supplier s ON s.s_nationkey = n.n_nationkey
    JOIN lineitem l1 ON l1.l_suppkey = s.s_suppkey
    JOIN orders o ON o.o_orderkey = l1.l_orderkey
    WHERE n.n_name = 'MOZAMBIQUE'
      AND o.o_orderstatus = 'F'
      AND l1.l_receiptdate > l1.l_commitdate
),
order_stats AS (
    SELECT
        l.l_orderkey,
        COUNT(DISTINCT l.l_suppkey) AS supplier_count,
        COUNT(DISTINCT l.l_suppkey) FILTER (WHERE l.l_receiptdate > l.l_commitdate) AS late_supplier_count,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE l.l_receiptdate > l.l_commitdate) AS late_line_count,
        MAX(l.l_suppkey) FILTER (WHERE l.l_receiptdate > l.l_commitdate) AS late_suppkey
    FROM lineitem l
    JOIN candidate_orders c ON c.l_orderkey = l.l_orderkey
    GROUP BY l.l_orderkey
)
SELECT
    s.s_name,
    SUM(os.late_line_count) AS numwait
FROM order_stats os
JOIN supplier s ON s.s_suppkey = os.late_suppkey
WHERE os.supplier_count > 1
  AND os.late_supplier_count = 1
GROUP BY s.s_name
ORDER BY numwait DESC, s.s_name
LIMIT 100;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Eliminate correlated EXISTS and NOT EXISTS subqueries on lineitem. Their semantics (order has >1 supplier and no other supplier with a late line) are replaced by per-order aggregation: supplier_count > 1 and late_supplier_count = 1. This removes the full parallel seq scan of lineitem l3 (anti-join) and per-row index probes into l2.

Early filtering: only orders containing a late lineitem from a MOZAMBIQUE supplier with o_orderstatus = 'F' can possibly qualify. These are pre-computed in candidate_orders, drastically reducing the rows the per-order aggregation must touch (nation selectivity ~1/25, late-line selectivity ~1/6).

Use conditional aggregation (COUNT(DISTINCT) FILTER, COUNT(*) FILTER, MAX() FILTER) to compute supplier_count, late_supplier_count, late_line_count and late_suppkey in one pass per candidate order. Since exactly one late supplier exists, all late lines in the order belong to it, so MAX(l_suppkey) FILTER identifies it and COUNT(*) FILTER counts its late lines — preserving exact equivalence with the original count(*).

Convert implicit comma joins to explicit ANSI JOINs and drive candidate_orders from the highly selective nation filter. The final join drops the redundant nation re-check: candidate_orders guarantees the unique late supplier is a MOZAMBIQUE supplier.
